### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained A19, A25 and A20, always in the order A19 → A25 → A20, entered from A41 (A41 led to A19 in about 96 in 100 of its outgoing transitions). In the later window, each of the three appears in only about 53–54 in 100 traces, and in about 46 in 100 traces none of them appears; they are almost never seen partially, and when they do run they keep the same internal order. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL022]
- In the later window, A41 leads directly to A26 in about 39 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (a connection not observed earlier), while A41 → A19 falls from about 96 to 47 in 100; accordingly, A26 now follows A41 within one event position in about 40 in 100 joint occurrences, versus essentially never before (it previously followed about four positions later). [DIR008, LAG008]
- The surrounding backbone is stable: A26, A46 and A47 still occur in essentially every trace in both windows, A20 still leads to A26 in about 97 in 100 of its transitions in both windows, and A46 still leads to A47 in about 97 in 100 before and 87 in 100 after. [DIR007, DIR010, POS003, LAG009]
- A06 drops from about 71 in 100 traces to about 26 in 100 and appears later in the trace (median event position about 0.16 to 0.30). Earlier, A14 led to A06 in about 69 in 100 of its transitions and A06 led on to A15 in about 92 in 100; in the later window A14 leads straight to A15 in about 78 in 100 (A06 only about 12 in 100), and A06's outgoing transitions are spread over many targets. [OCC002, POS001, DIR005, DIR003, REL001]
- A04, A08 and A10, previously present in about 4–5 in 100 traces, each appear in about 15–20 in 100 later traces (based on only 8–40 traces per window, so modest support). [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004]
- A14 and A15 still occur in every trace in both windows, and A15 still leads to A16 in about 93–98 in 100 of its transitions. [DIR006, POS002, REL013]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence directly and consistently supports the possibility that the segment A41 → A19 → A25 → A20 became optional: it ran in every earlier trace, while in the later window the three activities run in only about 53–54 in 100 traces, are skipped together in about 46 in 100 (almost never partially), keep their order and their entry from A41 whenever they run, and A41 then leads directly onward to A26. The unchanged exit and downstream behaviour (A20 still leads to A26 in about 97 in 100 of its transitions; A26, A46 and A47 still occur in every trace) supports "skipped" rather than "moved". Screening qualified 59 control-flow items where fewer than 1 would qualify without a change, so the ensemble is not what a stable process produces, and each item's difference also exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits. Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether individual cases skip the segment at random or because of case characteristics, and cannot rule out that the later window simply mixes case types in which the segment does not apply; incoming transitions were not measured, so what precedes A46/A47 when the segment is skipped is unknown. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL022, DIR008, LAG008, DIR007, DIR010, POS003]

Other differences: A06 changed from a frequent early step between A14 and A15 (71 in 100 traces, usually immediately after A14) into a rarer, later and loosely connected activity (26 in 100 traces), with A14 now usually bypassing it; A04, A08 and A10 occur about three to four times more often; A14 sits slightly later, the gap from A14 to A41 shortened by about one step, and the A46→A47 gap lengthened slightly. [OCC002, POS001, DIR003, DIR005, LAG003, LAG005, LAG009, OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, POS002]
